name: Dry Hills
summary: Witchwing harpies rule the green Dry Hills above the Barrens.

sections.title: A Green Haven for Harpies
sections.body: The Dry Hills rise along the Barrens’ northwestern edge, beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Their slopes are greener than the dry plains below, but the bluffs offer travelers little safety. Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing harpies from roosts along the crags. Their raiders swoop on supply caravans traveling the northern Gold Road. Abandoned orcish fortifications and derelict siege engines rot in the brush.

sections.title: Threat to the Crossroads
sections.body: Witchwing harpies strike from the hills to bleed trade routes and harass nearby settlements. So the Horde keeps a standing bounty on their feathers. Their nests and roosts are heavily defended in the rocky ravines. Hecklefang hyenas prowl there, while fierce Sunscale raptors hunt across the highlands.

faq.q: Why is it called the Dry Hills if it's so green?
faq.answer: Despite their name, the Dry Hills are noticeably greener than the surrounding Barrens. No record explains the name or the local contrast.

faq.q: Who lives in the Dry Hills?
faq.answer: The Witchwing tribe of harpies controls almost all the hills under Serena Bloodfeather’s rule. Hecklefang hyenas and Sunscale raptors also roam the rocky slopes.

faq.q: Why is the Horde interested in this area?
faq.answer: Witchwing raiders strike from the hills to plunder supply caravans on the northern Gold Road. Horde commanders issue bounties to cull their numbers and eliminate their leaders.

faq.q: What are the ruined towers and catapults in the middle of the hills?
faq.answer: The towers and catapults are the remains of an abandoned orcish outpost. The surviving structures do not reveal its original mission or why it was deserted.

angles.text: Witchwing harpies nesting in the Dry Hills threaten the northern trade routes linking the Crossroads to Stonetalon and Ashenvale. Horde champions must regularly cull them.
The rugged uplands offer rich hunting grounds. Swift Hecklefang hyenas, predatory Sunscale scytheclaws, and fierce harpies roam there.
